# `sec-ts/next-server-action-validation`

**A Next.js server action validates its input**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-security-ts` (npm) |
| **Languages** | TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `validators` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the schema and the authorisation check are written by the author) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Security** | CWE-20 · CWE-862 · OWASP A01:2025 · security severity `high` |

## What it checks

An exported function in a `"use server"` file that takes arguments calls a validator (`schema.parse`, `safeParse`, `validate`) on them.

**Your validator:** the function passes when it calls one of the `validators` anywhere in its body, or in a function around it: the built-in list (zod and valibot imports and a `*Schema.parse`, any `.safeParse`, `.parseAsync`, `.validate` or `.assert`, yup, joi, class-validator, class-transformer's `plainToInstance`, superstruct, typia) plus your own, each matched by name and by the module it is imported from, so a local `function validate(x) { return x }` does not count. `validators_mode = "replace"` makes yours the only ones that count. Add a project function with `validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]`. A validator that a helper calls for you is not seen: name the helper.

**Why:** A server action is a public HTTP endpoint: its arguments come from the client whatever the form looks like, so an unchecked one writes what an attacker sends (CWE-20, CWE-862). Whether the function also checks who is calling is not decided from the syntax.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-security-ts
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:sec-ts/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `validators` | `call[]` | 25 entries (below) | calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count |
| `validators_mode` | `string` | `"extend"` | `extend` adds your `validators` to the default list; `replace` uses only yours |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation"]
severity = "error"

[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "z.*", module = "zod" }, { name = "z.*.*", module = "zod" }, "*Schema.parse", "*schema.parse", "*.parseAsync", "*.safeParse", "*.safeParseAsync", { name = "v.*", module = "valibot" }, { name = "parse", module = "valibot" }, { name = "safeParse", module = "valibot" }, { name = "parseAsync", module = "valibot" }, { name = "yup.*", module = "yup" }, { name = "Joi.*", module = "joi" }, { name = "joi.*", module = "joi" }, "*.validate", "*.validateSync", "*.validateAsync", { name = "validate", module = ["class-validator", "superstruct"] }, { name = "validateOrReject", module = "class-validator" }, { name = "validateSync", module = "class-validator" }, { name = "plainToInstance", module = "class-transformer" }, { name = "assert", module = "superstruct" }, { name = "create", module = "superstruct" }, "*.assert", { name = "typia.*", module = "typia" }]
validators_mode = "extend"
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = { severity = "error", options = { validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep, except a `call[]` option in `extend` mode, which adds to it.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `validators`

*call[]* · default: the list below

calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
```

**The default list** — a callee path (a global, `*.` for any receiver) or `{ name, module }`, held only when imported from that module:

```toml
validators = [
  { name = "z.*", module = "zod" },
  { name = "z.*.*", module = "zod" },
  "*Schema.parse",
  "*schema.parse",
  "*.parseAsync",
  "*.safeParse",
  "*.safeParseAsync",
  { name = "v.*", module = "valibot" },
  { name = "parse", module = "valibot" },
  { name = "safeParse", module = "valibot" },
  { name = "parseAsync", module = "valibot" },
  { name = "yup.*", module = "yup" },
  { name = "Joi.*", module = "joi" },
  { name = "joi.*", module = "joi" },
  "*.validate",
  "*.validateSync",
  "*.validateAsync",
  { name = "validate", module = ["class-validator", "superstruct"] },
  { name = "validateOrReject", module = "class-validator" },
  { name = "validateSync", module = "class-validator" },
  { name = "plainToInstance", module = "class-transformer" },
  { name = "assert", module = "superstruct" },
  { name = "create", module = "superstruct" },
  "*.assert",
  { name = "typia.*", module = "typia" },
]
```

**Only yours count** — a direct call to a default entry is then reported:

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
validators_mode = "replace"
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/security-ts/rules/sec-ts/next-server-action-validation.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### extend: the project validator and the built-in both pass

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
```

```ts
"use server";
import { checkInput } from "@acme/validation";
export async function f(input: unknown) {
  await save(checkInput(input));
}
export async function g(input: unknown) {
  await save(postSchema.parse(input));
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### replace: only the project validator passes

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
validators_mode = "replace"
```

```ts
"use server";
import { checkInput } from "@acme/validation";
export async function f(input: unknown) {
  await save(checkInput(input));
}
export async function g(input: unknown) {
  await save(postSchema.parse(input));
}
```

**Reports** at `6:8`.

#### an aliased import passes

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
validators_mode = "replace"
```

```ts
"use server";
import { checkInput as check } from "@acme/validation";
export async function f(input: unknown) {
  await save(check(input));
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a same-named local function is reported

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
```

```ts
"use server";
function checkInput(x: unknown) { return x; }
export async function f(input: unknown) {
  await save(checkInput(input));
}
```

**Reports** at `3:8`.

#### the wrong module is reported

```toml
[rules."sec-ts/next-server-action-validation".options]
validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }]
```

```ts
"use server";
import { checkInput } from "@other/validation";
export async function f(input: unknown) {
  await save(checkInput(input));
}
```

**Reports** at `3:8`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = { options = { validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"sec-ts/next-server-action-validation" = { severity = "warn", options = { validators = [{ name = "checkInput", module = "@acme/validation" }] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "sec-ts/next-server-action-validation": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"validators": [{"name": "checkInput", "module": "@acme/validation"}]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **TypeScript:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-ts/next-server-action-validation: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-ts/next-server-action-validation expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule sec-ts/next-server-action-validation --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain sec-ts/next-server-action-validation       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule sec-ts/next-server-action-validation  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                        # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Parse the arguments with a schema (`zod`, `valibot`) at the top of the action and use the parsed value only.
2. Check the caller next: read the session and refuse when the user may not do this (`const session = await auth(); if (!session) throw …`).
3. Return a small, typed result; never return a database row whole.

## Examples

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
"use server";
export async function createPost(input: FormData) {
  await db.insert(posts).values({ title: String(input.get("title")) });
}
```

#### Do

```ts
"use server";
export async function createPost(input: FormData) {
  const data = postSchema.parse({ title: input.get("title") });
  await db.insert(posts).values(data);
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
"use server";
export async function createPost(input: FormData) {
  await db.insert(posts).values({ title: String(input.get("title")) });
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
"use server";
export async function createPost(input: FormData) {
  const data = postSchema.parse({ title: input.get("title") });
  await db.insert(posts).values(data);
}
```
